## PART 3: FIVE TATA STEEL-SPECIFIC BULLET REWRITES

Use these verbatim in any Tata Steel-targeted writing.

**Bullet 1 — Multi-agent orchestration**
Designed and deployed a 93-agent AI orchestration platform using Claude Agent SDK and FastAPI; parallel worker dispatch via asyncio.gather enables concurrent multi-domain task execution across 11 integrated toolkits — the same fan-out architecture Tata Steel operates across defect detection, predictive maintenance, and process optimization at global scale.

**Bullet 2 — Safety framework**
Engineered a 4-tier safety enforcement system for autonomous AI actions: Tier 1 fully auto, Tier 2 auto with immutable audit log, Tier 3 human-confirm required for all irreversible operations, Tier 4 permanent refuse; Tier-3 actions including external API calls, form submissions, and destructive file ops never execute without explicit human approval even in fullauto mode.

**Bullet 3 — Autonomous goal lifecycle**
Built an autonomous goal execution engine: natural-language goal intake → LLM decomposition into typed sub-tasks (JSON-schema validated) → parallel Tier-1/2 execution → human-approval queue for Tier-3 → morning digest; per-goal $5 budget cap and 2-hour duration cap with automatic FAIL state and orphan recovery on daemon restart — same governance model required when AI proposes maintenance actions with cost and SLA constraints.

**Bullet 4 — Episodic memory and RAG**
Shipped production episodic memory layer: ChromaDB vector store, sentence-transformers embeddings, 155-chunk bootstrap + daily incremental ingestion, semantic recall injected into every agent invocation (threshold 0.55, top-5 chunks, 2000-token cap) — same retrieval-augmented architecture behind Tata Steel's TDA enterprise assistant and customer complaint classification systems.

**Bullet 5 — Continuous improvement loop**
Deployed a weekly self-improvement loop: LLM synthesizes signals from feedback logs, eval baselines, and agent invocation traces → proposes capability-change patches → auto-applies Tier-1/2 safe changes → holds Tier-3 for human review; eval regression gate (>5pp pass-rate drop suspends auto-apply) ensures the platform does not degrade in production — same continuous improvement discipline required to keep 550+ production models performing reliably.

**The only real gap: Steel and manufacturing domain knowledge.**

What it means concretely: no hot strip mill ops knowledge, no blast furnace chemistry, no SCADA/historian DB experience, no steel surface defect taxonomy (pits, cracks, rolled-in scale, edge seams), no silicon content prediction window context.
